title: [Classic Long-Form RPG] Reflecting on Console RPG Maker

blocks.source: 【王道長編RPG】家庭用ツクールに思いを馳せて
blocks.translation: [Classic Long-Form RPG] Reflecting on Console RPG Maker

blocks.source: なんとなくカタツムリは自爆します。殻の中に爆薬が詰まっているようなイメージ。
blocks.translation: For some reason, the snails self-destruct. Imagine their shells being packed with explosives.

blocks.source: 奥義の仕様はこんな感じになりました。ボス戦で開幕奥義連発はできません。実際にやってみたら、開幕から長めのアニメーションが続くのでテンポ悪いです。レベルが想定より高めだと一気に決着がついてしまったりで、感覚的に「これはいかん」と思ったので制約をかけました。
blocks.translation: The Arts specifications have turned out like this. You cannot unleash a series of Arts at the start of a boss battle. When I actually tried it, the lengthy animations continued from the opening, which made the pacing feel poor. If the level was higher than expected, the battle could also end all at once, and I instinctively thought, “This isn’t right,” so I placed restrictions on them.

blocks.source: 二周目のテストプレイ途中ですが、さすがにもう細かい調整ばかりで書くことがあまりありませんね。『お金』『魔石』『スキルポイント』といったゲーム全体を通して調節が必要なリソースの設定に苦労しています。
blocks.translation: I’m partway through the second test playthrough, but by this point there isn’t much left to write about, since it’s mostly fine-tuning. I’m struggling with setting resources that need to be adjusted throughout the game, such as “money,” “magic stones,” and “skill points.”

blocks.source: ところで最近はニコ動の『他人ツクールシリーズ』を見ながら制作をしています。
blocks.translation: By the way, lately I’ve been working while watching NicoNico’s “Other People’s RPG Maker Series.”

blocks.source: 中古で買ってきたり、投稿されてきた家庭用ＲＰＧツクール作品（主に１，２）の実況動画なのですが、意外性があって面白いです。それこそ「城が消えるだけ」の作品から、そこそこの中長編作品があったりと千差万別です。
blocks.translation: These are commentary videos of console RPG Maker games bought secondhand or submitted by users (mainly RPG Maker 1 and 2), and they’re surprisingly entertaining. They vary widely, from games where “the castle simply disappears” to fairly decent medium- and long-form games.

blocks.source: マイリスト（※注：かなりの長寿シリーズであるため超絶長いです。）
blocks.translation: My List (※Note: Since this is an extremely long-running series, it’s incredibly long.)

blocks.source: http://www.nicovideo.jp/mylist/7938167
blocks.translation: http://www.nicovideo.jp/mylist/7938167

blocks.source: まとめWiki
blocks.translation: Compilation Wiki

blocks.source: http://www14.atwiki.jp/taninrpg/pages/1.html
blocks.translation: http://www14.atwiki.jp/taninrpg/pages/1.html

blocks.source: それなりに完成度の高そうな作品がエターなっていたりで、まともに完成していることのありがたさがよ～く分かります。そしてそのエターなった作品をリメイクしている人もいたりで、再生数の割にファンが多く、影響度も高いことが伺えます。
blocks.translation: Some works that seemed to have a fairly high level of polish had been abandoned, which really makes me appreciate how fortunate it is when something is properly completed. Some people even remake those abandoned works, suggesting that they have many fans and considerable influence despite their view counts.

blocks.source: 僕もＳＦＣの初代ＲＰＧツクールから始めた口なので、実に懐かしい気分になりました。当時はストーリーもメチャクチャな上に、ゲームバランスの取り方もつかめず変なものを量産していた覚えがあります。
blocks.translation: I also started with the original RPG Maker for the SNES, so it made me feel truly nostalgic. Back then, not only were the stories a complete mess, but I also couldn’t figure out how to balance the games, and I remember mass-producing all sorts of strange things.

blocks.source: 何だかんだで完成まではさせるのですが……
blocks.translation: Somehow, I did always manage to finish them, though…

blocks.source: 最初のダンジョンがラストダンジョン。
blocks.translation: The first dungeon is the final dungeon.

blocks.source: 魔王城は予算の都合で一フロアしかない。
blocks.translation: The Demon Lord’s Castle has only one floor due to budget constraints.

blocks.source: 魔王が家庭の事情で戦闘放棄。
blocks.translation: The Demon Lord abandons the battle because of family circumstances.

blocks.source: 主人公の母親が突如裏切ってラスボス化。
blocks.translation: The protagonist’s mother suddenly betrays them and becomes the final boss.

blocks.source: ラスボスを倒した主人公が戦利品（ラスボスのブロマイド）のしょぼさに嘆いて身投げする。
blocks.translation: After defeating the final boss, the protagonist throws themself to their death, lamenting how pathetic the spoils of war (a bromide photo of the final boss) are.

blocks.source: などなど、酷い締めくくり方をした記憶が多数あります。
blocks.translation: And so on—I have many memories of ending things in terrible ways.

blocks.source: ただそんなのでも、無理矢理オチをつけて終わらせるということを繰り返していれば「まともに完成させるにはどうしたらいいか？」という現実も見えてくるものです。２時間の短編を完成させた経験があれば、５時間の中編を完成させる労力も何となく想像できるようになってきます。経験とは大事ですね。
blocks.translation: Even with works like those, if you repeatedly force an ending onto them and bring them to a close, you eventually begin to see the reality of “What should I do to complete something properly?” Once you have the experience of completing a two-hour short game, you can start to imagine, at least vaguely, the effort required to complete a five-hour medium-length game. Experience really is important.

blocks.source: ちなみにＳＦＣ時代の作品についてはデータが残っていないのですが、ＰＳのツクール３，４についてはメモリーカードに残っていました。酷いストーリーですがゲームとしてはわりとまともに遊べるはずです。そのうちデータだけでも公開しましょうか。
blocks.translation: Incidentally, I no longer have the data for my works from the SNES era, but my RPG Maker 3 and 4 games for the PlayStation were still saved on memory cards. The stories are terrible, but they should be reasonably playable as games. Perhaps I’ll release just the data someday.

blocks.source: 話を戻して、動画にある作品は荒いゲームバランスの作品が多いのですが、それでも何とかなってしまうところも面白い。ボスが即死級の攻撃をしかけてくるが、蘇生アイテムで強引に押し切れたりします。
blocks.translation: Returning to the subject, many of the games in the videos have rough game balance, but it’s also interesting how they somehow still work. A boss may unleash attacks capable of instantly killing you, yet you can sometimes force your way through with revival items.

blocks.source: 二章のボス、サイコゴーレムが強すぎる。
blocks.translation: The Chapter Two boss, Psycho Golem, is far too strong.

blocks.source: 二章限定キャラとはいえ、なぜかネモが最強。
blocks.translation: Despite being a Chapter Two–only character, Nemo is inexplicably the strongest.

blocks.source: こんなガンダムゲーがかつてあっただろうか。
blocks.translation: Could there ever have been a Gundam game like this?

blocks.source: 三章の序盤アムロ一人旅が難しすぎる。敵の強さが一人旅を想定していない。
blocks.translation: The solo journey with Amuro at the beginning of Chapter Three is far too difficult. The enemies’ strength doesn’t account for traveling alone.

blocks.source: なにこれクソゲー――と言われても仕方のないバランスではあるのですが、それを試行錯誤しながら、乗り越えるのに妙な達成感があったりしました。難易度が安定しているだけがゲームバランスではない。荒さが味になることもあるのだなあと、子供心に妙に納得した記憶があります。
blocks.translation: The balance is bad enough that you can’t blame someone for saying, “What is this piece of crap?!” Yet struggling through it by trial and error gave me a strange sense of accomplishment. Game balance isn’t just about keeping the difficulty consistent. I remember, in my childish way, being oddly convinced that roughness can sometimes become part of a game’s charm.

blocks.source: 制作講座には「簡単でも難しくもないことが良いゲームバランスとは限らない」的なことを書いたはずですが、それはこの辺の経験から来ています。むしろ、ゲームの進行によって、多少の難易度変動があるほうが、メリハリがあってよいのではないでしょうか。例えば、どうでもよいダンジョンは難易度を下げて、重要なダンジョンは上げる――という感じです。
blocks.translation: I believe I wrote something in the RPG Design Guides along the lines of “A game isn’t necessarily well-balanced just because it is neither easy nor difficult,” and that idea comes from experiences like these. Rather, wouldn’t a game be more engaging if its difficulty varied somewhat as the game progressed, giving it more contrast? For example, you could lower the difficulty of unimportant dungeons and raise it for important ones—the idea being something like that.

blocks.source: なので、どのダンジョン＆ボスも入念に時間をかけて、難易度を調整するということは昔からやっていません。山場に時間をかけて、単なる繋ぎのダンジョン＆ボスは適当にすることが多いです。ボスの能力や行動パターンをわざと雑にすることもよくあります。
blocks.translation: That’s why I’ve never spent a great deal of time carefully adjusting the difficulty of every dungeon and boss. I tend to spend time on major set pieces and handle simple transitional dungeons and bosses more casually. I also often deliberately make a boss’s abilities or behavior patterns rough around the edges.

blocks.source: というのも能力・行動パターンが緻密で隙のないボスって、返って面白みがない場合も多いのですよね。様々な攻撃をしかけてくる相手には、対策が取りにくくなるわけで、そうなると結局、「回復しながら攻撃する」ぐらいしかやりようがなくなったりするわけです。
blocks.translation: The reason is that bosses with meticulously designed abilities and behavior patterns, without any openings, are often less interesting. When an opponent uses a wide variety of attacks, it becomes difficult to devise countermeasures, and in the end you may be left with little to do besides “attack while healing.”

blocks.source: そこで時には、一つの技しか使わないという手抜き半分の極端なボスを出してみると、意外なアクセントになったりします。見え見えの攻撃にどう対処するかというのは、結構プレイヤースキルが求められるものだったりしますので。
blocks.translation: So sometimes, introducing an extreme boss that only uses one skill—partly as a shortcut—can provide an unexpected change of pace. Figuring out how to deal with an obvious attack can actually demand a fair amount of player skill.

blocks.source: でも、ラスボスが一つの技しか使わないＦＦ３（ＦＣ）は思い切り良すぎですね。
blocks.translation: Still, FF3 (FC), whose final boss uses only one skill, takes things a little too far.

blocks.source: で、そんな経験を踏まえた上でミスタことMystic Starは何を目指すかというと、色んな要素を盛り込みながらも、バランスが崩れないということが目標です。
blocks.translation: So, taking those experiences into account, what does Mystic Star, or “Mista,” aim for? Its goal is to incorporate all sorts of elements without throwing the balance off.

blocks.source: 成長システムの自由度を高めると、キャラの個性が乏しくなる。同時に誰でも様々な技が使えることから、バランスが崩れやすい。ＤＱ６～７の特技連発など。
blocks.translation: Increasing the freedom of the growth system diminishes the characters’ individuality. At the same time, because anyone can use a variety of Techs, the balance becomes easy to disrupt. For example, the endless Tech use in DQ6–7.

blocks.source: かといって、キャラの個性を尖らせてインパクトある固有技を覚えさせても、やはりバランスが崩れやすい。キャラ間のバランスを取るのも大変。
blocks.translation: On the other hand, even if you sharpen the characters’ individuality and teach them impactful unique skills, the balance is still easy to disrupt. Maintaining balance between the characters is also difficult.

blocks.source: このようなジレンマというのは、ゲーム制作にはしょっちゅうつきまとうもの。ただゲームバランスを安定させたいなら、成長システムを制限し、キャラクターの個性も程々に抑えればよいわけですが、それで面白いかどうかは別問題です。
blocks.translation: This kind of dilemma is something that constantly follows game development. If you simply want to stabilize the game balance, you can restrict the growth system and keep the characters’ individuality within reasonable limits, but whether the result is interesting is another matter.

blocks.source: 「二兎を追う者は一兎をも得ず」といわれている通り、慣れないうちは方向を絞ったほうがよいかもしれません。……が、今回はあえてできる限りの両立に挑戦しています。
blocks.translation: As the saying goes, “If you chase two rabbits, you will catch neither,” so it may be better to narrow your focus while you’re inexperienced. …But this time, I’m deliberately challenging myself to achieve both as much as possible.

blocks.source: 無難にはせず尖った要素も取り入れる。しかしバランスも壊さないというのはなかなか難しい。市販ＲＰＧでもこれができている作品なんて、なかなかあるものではありません。
blocks.translation: I won’t play it safe; I’ll incorporate some distinctive elements. But maintaining the balance at the same time is quite difficult. Even among commercially released RPGs, there aren’t many games that manage to do this.

blocks.source: 特に戦略・戦術の自由度が高い尖った作品は、ゲーム後半になるほどバランス崩壊を起こしやすくなります。まさにＦＦシリーズがよくやってますよね。
blocks.translation: In particular, distinctive games with a high degree of freedom in strategy and tactics are prone to their balance collapsing as the latter half of the game approaches. The FF series does this quite often, doesn’t it?

blocks.source: となると無難寄りの安定ゲームバランスとしてＤＱシリーズが挙げられます。特にＤＱ３（特にＦＣ）とＤＱ４（特にＰＳ）はその代表格でしょう。ＤＱ５～７において、様々な要素が導入されていくにつれ、バランスが崩れていくのも、まさにこのジレンマを体現しているかのようです。
blocks.translation: In that case, the DQ series can be cited as an example of a stable, relatively safe game balance. DQ3 (especially the FC version) and DQ4 (especially the PS version) are probably prime examples. In DQ5–7, the way the balance breaks down as various elements are introduced seems almost to embody this very dilemma.

blocks.source: 個人的にこれが現状で最も両立ができているのはサガシリーズだと思っています。「戦略性の高さ」「後半のボス戦の熱さ」と両方に定評があるのは特筆すべきことです。
blocks.translation: Personally, I think the SaGa series currently does the best job of achieving both. It’s noteworthy that the series is highly regarded for both its “strategic depth” and the “intensity of its later boss battles.”

blocks.source: この辺、当作においては『奥義』がなかなか良い感じに機能しているように思います。一見、バランスを壊しかねないほど強力な効果であっても、使用条件を制限することで抑制できます。奥義発動のタイミングを考える必要があるため、単調なダメージの与え合いを崩すことを期待しています。
blocks.translation: In this respect, I feel that Arts are working quite well in this game. Even effects that seem powerful enough at first glance to risk breaking the balance can be kept in check by restricting their usage conditions. Since you have to consider when to activate an Art, I hope they will break up the monotonous exchange of damage.

blocks.source: というわけで、１４４０時間経過です。若干ペースが落ちてますが、どうも完成を意識しだした影響のようです。完成度を高めるにはどうしたらよいか――ということを考え、色んなことを気にしながらテストプレイをしていると、どうしても消耗は早くなるみたいです。自然、息抜きしたくなったり。
blocks.translation: And so, 1,440 hours have passed. My pace has slowed a little, apparently because I’ve started thinking more consciously about finishing. When I test-play while thinking about how to improve the level of polish and worrying about all sorts of things, I seem to wear myself out more quickly. Naturally, I start wanting to take a break.

blocks.source: 制作途中は「完成を強く意識せず、日課を楽しむように淡々とやる」という感じだったのですが、それがうまくいっていたのでしょう。
blocks.translation: During development, my approach was to “work steadily, without thinking too intensely about finishing, and enjoy it as part of my daily routine.” Perhaps that was working well for me.

blocks.source: 以前書いた持論とも符合しますが、制作序盤～中盤から完成を意識しすぎて必死になってしまう人は消耗のために、エターなりやすいのだと思います。ご注意ください。
blocks.translation: This also agrees with an opinion I wrote about before, but I think people who become desperate by focusing too much on finishing from the early to middle stages of development are more likely to abandon their projects because of exhaustion. Please be careful.

blocks.source: 思い返せば、今回に限らず過去の作品も制作終盤はそんな感じだった気がします。長編は一周するだけで大変です。その上、自分の作品は知り尽くしているため、何周もクリアしたゲームをやっているような飽きた気分になりがちです。それで「もういいや」って感じになっちゃうんですよね。
blocks.translation: Looking back, I feel that the late stages of my past works—not just this one—were probably like that too. It’s hard enough just to play through a long-form game once. On top of that, because I know my own works inside and out, I tend to feel bored, as if I were playing a game I had already cleared many times. That makes me feel like, “I’ve had enough.”

blocks.source: 中には自分の作品をテストプレイしてみて「思ったよりつまらないかも……」と感じて悩む人もいるかもしれません。ですが、わりとこの現象は誰にでもあることだと思うので、強く気にしないことをお勧めします。
blocks.translation: Some people may test-play their own work, feel “Maybe it’s more boring than I thought…,” and worry about it. However, I think this phenomenon happens to just about everyone, so I recommend not worrying about it too much.

blocks.source: 何はともあれ、今回は今までより慎重にいきたいので、適度に息抜きしながらやっていきたいと思っています。幸い過去の作品よりはテストプレイを楽しめている感じです。パーティ編成、装備、スキル、行き先の自由度があるので、二周目でも感覚が違うのが大きいですね。
blocks.translation: In any case, I want to be more careful this time than I have been before, so I plan to continue while taking breaks in moderation. Fortunately, I feel that I’m enjoying test play more than I did with my past works. There is freedom in party composition, equipment, skills, and where to go, so even the second playthrough feels quite different.

lines.source: 荒いゲームバランスで思い返すのが、ＳＦＣの[[LINK_1]]ナイトガンダム物語[[/LINK_1]]。全体的にはそこまで高難易度のＲＰＧではないのですが、ムラがあって突如難易度がインフレするゲームでした。

parts.source: 荒いゲームバランスで思い返すのが、ＳＦＣの

texts.なにこれクソゲー――と言われても仕方のないバランスではあるのですが、それを試行錯: The balance is bad enough that you can’t blame someone for saying, “What is this piece of crap?!” Yet struggling through it by trial and error gave me a strange sense of accomplishment. Game balance isn’t just about keeping the difficulty consistent. I remember, in my childish way, being oddly convinced that roughness can sometimes become part of a game’s charm.
texts.制作講座には「簡単でも難しくもないことが良いゲームバランスとは限らない」的なこと: I believe I wrote something in the RPG Design Guides along the lines of “A game isn’t necessarily well-balanced just because it is neither easy nor difficult,” and that idea comes from experiences like these. Rather, wouldn’t a game be more engaging if its difficulty varied somewhat as the game progressed, giving it more contrast? For example, you could lower the difficulty of unimportant dungeons and raise it for important ones—the idea being something like that.
texts.なので、どのダンジョン＆ボスも入念に時間をかけて、難易度を調整するということは昔: That’s why I’ve never spent a great deal of time carefully adjusting the difficulty of every dungeon and boss. I tend to spend time on major set pieces and handle simple transitional dungeons and bosses more casually. I also often deliberately make a boss’s abilities or behavior patterns rough around the edges.
texts.というのも能力・行動パターンが緻密で隙のないボスって、返って面白みがない場合も多: The reason is that bosses with meticulously designed abilities and behavior patterns, without any openings, are often less interesting. When an opponent uses a wide variety of attacks, it becomes difficult to devise countermeasures, and in the end you may be left with little to do besides “attack while healing.”
texts.そこで時には、一つの技しか使わないという手抜き半分の極端なボスを出してみると、意: So sometimes, introducing an extreme boss that only uses one skill—partly as a shortcut—can provide an unexpected change of pace. Figuring out how to deal with an obvious attack can actually demand a fair amount of player skill.
texts.でも、ラスボスが一つの技しか使わないＦＦ３（ＦＣ）は思い切り良すぎですね。: Still, FF3 (FC), whose final boss uses only one skill, takes things a little too far.
texts.で、そんな経験を踏まえた上でミスタことMystic Starは何を目指すかという: So, taking those experiences into account, what does Mystic Star, or “Mista,” aim for? Its goal is to incorporate all sorts of elements without throwing the balance off.
texts.成長システムの自由度を高めると、キャラの個性が乏しくなる。同時に誰でも様々な技が: Increasing the freedom of the growth system diminishes the characters’ individuality. At the same time, because anyone can use a variety of Techs, the balance becomes easy to disrupt. For example, the endless Tech use in DQ6–7.
texts.かといって、キャラの個性を尖らせてインパクトある固有技を覚えさせても、やはりバラ: On the other hand, even if you sharpen the characters’ individuality and teach them impactful unique skills, the balance is still easy to disrupt. Maintaining balance between the characters is also difficult.
texts.このようなジレンマというのは、ゲーム制作にはしょっちゅうつきまとうもの。ただゲー: This kind of dilemma is something that constantly follows game development. If you simply want to stabilize the game balance, you can restrict the growth system and keep the characters’ individuality within reasonable limits, but whether the result is interesting is another matter.
texts.「二兎を追う者は一兎をも得ず」といわれている通り、慣れないうちは方向を絞ったほう: As the saying goes, “If you chase two rabbits, you will catch neither,” so it may be better to narrow your focus while you’re inexperienced. …But this time, I’m deliberately challenging myself to achieve both as much as possible.
texts.無難にはせず尖った要素も取り入れる。しかしバランスも壊さないというのはなかなか難: I won’t play it safe; I’ll incorporate some distinctive elements. But maintaining the balance at the same time is quite difficult. Even among commercially released RPGs, there aren’t many games that manage to do this.
texts.特に戦略・戦術の自由度が高い尖った作品は、ゲーム後半になるほどバランス崩壊を起こ: In particular, distinctive games with a high degree of freedom in strategy and tactics are prone to their balance collapsing as the latter half of the game approaches. The FF series does this quite often, doesn’t it?
texts.となると無難寄りの安定ゲームバランスとしてＤＱシリーズが挙げられます。特にＤＱ３: In that case, the DQ series can be cited as an example of a stable, relatively safe game balance. DQ3 (especially the FC version) and DQ4 (especially the PS version) are probably prime examples. In DQ5–7, the way the balance breaks down as various elements are introduced seems almost to embody this very dilemma.
texts.個人的にこれが現状で最も両立ができているのはサガシリーズだと思っています。「戦略: Personally, I think the SaGa series currently does the best job of achieving both. It’s noteworthy that the series is highly regarded for both its “strategic depth” and the “intensity of its later boss battles.”
texts.この辺、当作においては『奥義』がなかなか良い感じに機能しているように思います。一: In this respect, I feel that Arts are working quite well in this game. Even effects that seem powerful enough at first glance to risk breaking the balance can be kept in check by restricting their usage conditions. Since you have to consider when to activate an Art, I hope they will break up the monotonous exchange of damage.
texts.というわけで、１４４０時間経過です。若干ペースが落ちてますが、どうも完成を意識し: And so, 1,440 hours have passed. My pace has slowed a little, apparently because I’ve started thinking more consciously about finishing. When I test-play while thinking about how to improve the level of polish and worrying about all sorts of things, I seem to wear myself out more quickly. Naturally, I start wanting to take a break.
texts.制作途中は「完成を強く意識せず、日課を楽しむように淡々とやる」という感じだったの: During development, my approach was to “work steadily, without thinking too intensely about finishing, and enjoy it as part of my daily routine.” Perhaps that was working well for me.
texts.以前書いた持論とも符合しますが、制作序盤～中盤から完成を意識しすぎて必死になって: This also agrees with an opinion I wrote about before, but I think people who become desperate by focusing too much on finishing from the early to middle stages of development are more likely to abandon their projects because of exhaustion. Please be careful.
texts.思い返せば、今回に限らず過去の作品も制作終盤はそんな感じだった気がします。長編は: Looking back, I feel that the late stages of my past works—not just this one—were probably like that too. It’s hard enough just to play through a long-form game once. On top of that, because I know my own works inside and out, I tend to feel bored, as if I were playing a game I had already cleared many times. That makes me feel like, “I’ve had enough.”
texts.中には自分の作品をテストプレイしてみて「思ったよりつまらないかも……」と感じて悩: Some people may test-play their own work, feel “Maybe it’s more boring than I thought…,” and worry about it. However, I think this phenomenon happens to just about everyone, so I recommend not worrying about it too much.
texts.何はともあれ、今回は今までより慎重にいきたいので、適度に息抜きしながらやっていき: In any case, I want to be more careful this time than I have been before, so I plan to continue while taking breaks in moderation. Fortunately, I feel that I’m enjoying test play more than I did with my past works. There is freedom in party composition, equipment, skills, and where to go, so even the second playthrough feels quite different.
